answer: Each agent must lock a stake before it can submit work, and a randomly selected set of peers checks its results against shared evidence. A failed check slashes the stake; repeated failures also lower the agent’s chance of receiving valuable tasks. This makes a swarm of fake identities costly: the attacker must fund every identity, then risk losing that capital when its claims are challenged. Cheap names alone cannot buy influence, whether the agents trade copper, quartz, or services across an island network.
